title: Acute Sleep Deprivation
interpretation: A single night with less than 5 hours of total sleep significantly impairs cognitive function, reaction time, and emotional regulation. Effects are measurable the following day in elevated stress scores, reduced HRV, and increased resting heart rate. One bad night is recoverable; consecutive nights compound the effects.
recommended_agent_action: Log as single occurrence. If user slept less than 5 hours, note it as context for the following day's vital interpretation. Do not alert for a single night.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude insomnia from a single poor night. Occasional poor sleep is normal.
sources: Journal of Sleep Research - Acute Sleep Loss

title: Chronic Sleep Deficit Pattern
interpretation: Sleep totaling less than 6 hours per night for 7+ consecutive days creates a cumulative sleep debt. Effects include impaired immune function, increased cortisol, weight gain tendency, and measurably lower cognitive performance. Deep sleep percentage typically drops as the deficit accumulates.
recommended_agent_action: If average sleep drops below 6 hours for 7+ consecutive days, escalate to Level 3. Suggest sleep hygiene improvements and ask if external factors are contributing.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose chronic insomnia or sleep disorder. Some individuals naturally require less sleep (short sleeper phenotype).

title: Deep Sleep Deficit
interpretation: Deep sleep (N3/slow-wave sleep) is critical for physical recovery, immune function, and memory consolidation. Normal adults spend 15-25% of sleep in deep sleep. A sustained decline below 10% suggests disrupted sleep architecture, which can be caused by stress, alcohol, aging, or sleep disorders.
recommended_agent_action: Track deep sleep percentage trend. If below 10% for 5+ nights, flag as pattern. Cross-reference with alcohol use, stress scores, and medication changes.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose sleep architecture disorders. Deep sleep naturally decreases with age, especially after age 60.
sources: Sleep Medicine Reviews - Deep Sleep Function

title: Sleep Fragmentation
interpretation: Sleep efficiency below 75% combined with 4+ wake episodes per night indicates significant sleep fragmentation. Fragmented sleep fails to provide the restorative benefits of consolidated sleep even if total hours are adequate. Common causes include pain, nocturia, anxiety, and sleep-disordered breathing.
recommended_agent_action: Track sleep fragmentation over multiple nights. If pattern persists for 5+ nights, flag and ask user about potential causes (bathroom visits, pain, noise, anxiety).
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose sleep disorders from wake count alone. Brief awakenings are normal and often not remembered.
sources: Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine - Sleep Fragmentation

title: REM Sleep Reduction
interpretation: REM sleep constitutes 20-25% of total sleep in healthy adults and is essential for emotional processing, memory consolidation, and cognitive function. Sustained REM below 15% may indicate alcohol use, certain medications (SSRIs, benzodiazepines), or high stress levels suppressing REM entry.
recommended_agent_action: Monitor REM percentage trends. If below 15% for multiple nights, note as insight. Cross-reference with medication list and stress scores.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not attribute REM reduction to a specific cause without additional context. Many medications legitimately suppress REM sleep.
sources: Nature Reviews Neuroscience - REM Sleep Function

title: Prolonged Sleep Onset Latency
interpretation: Normal sleep onset latency is 10-20 minutes. Consistently taking more than 30 minutes to fall asleep suggests sleep-onset difficulty, which can be caused by anxiety, caffeine, irregular sleep schedule, or conditioned arousal. Paradoxically, very short onset (under 5 minutes) may indicate severe sleep deprivation.
recommended_agent_action: Track sleep onset trend. If consistently above 30 minutes for 5+ nights, suggest sleep hygiene practices. If under 5 minutes consistently, flag as potential sleep debt.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose insomnia from sleep onset time alone. Environmental and behavioral factors play a major role.
sources: Journal of Psychosomatic Research - Sleep Onset

title: Stress-Sleep Feedback Loop
interpretation: Elevated stress scores during the day predict poor sleep quality that night. Poor sleep in turn elevates the next day's stress response. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle that can escalate over days. Breaking the cycle typically requires intervention on either the stress or the sleep side.
recommended_agent_action: If both stress scores and sleep quality are declining simultaneously for 5+ days, flag as stress-sleep feedback loop. Provide actionable suggestions for breaking the cycle.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume the user cannot break this cycle on their own. Many people respond well to simple interventions.

title: Inadequate Recovery Sleep for Active Users
interpretation: Physically active individuals require more deep sleep for muscular repair and glycogen replenishment. If an active user's deep sleep drops below 15% while maintaining high activity levels, recovery will be compromised. This is reflected in declining recovery scores even with adequate total sleep hours.
recommended_agent_action: For active users with declining deep sleep and recovery scores, suggest adjusting training intensity or improving sleep conditions (cooler room, earlier bedtime).
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude overtraining from sleep metrics alone. Training logs and subjective fatigue must be considered.
sources: Sports Medicine - Sleep and Athletic Recovery

title: Elevated Nighttime Vitals During Sleep
interpretation: Heart rate and breathing rate that remain elevated during sleep (above daytime resting levels) suggest the body is not achieving adequate parasympathetic recovery. This pattern is associated with illness onset, high stress load, alcohol consumption, or sleep-disordered breathing.
recommended_agent_action: Cross-reference nighttime HR and breathing rate with daytime baselines. If nighttime values exceed daytime resting by 15%+, flag as concern and monitor for additional symptoms.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose sleep disorders from nighttime vital elevation alone. Many transient factors can cause this pattern.

title: Weekend Sleep Rebound Pattern
interpretation: Sleeping significantly more on weekends (2+ hours more than weekday average) indicates accumulated weekday sleep debt. While catch-up sleep provides some recovery, it cannot fully compensate for chronic weekday deprivation and disrupts circadian rhythm, creating a social jet lag effect.
recommended_agent_action: Track weekday vs weekend sleep differential. If difference exceeds 2 hours consistently, note as insight about sleep debt accumulation.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude pathology from weekend sleep rebound. It is a common and largely benign compensatory behavior.
